_comment: Per-chart narratives. CI (build_prompt.py -> GitHub Models -> write_narrative.py) overwrites these from live numbers; this committed copy is the fallback so the page always reads well. source = 'fallback' | 'github-models'.

notes.basket: The breakfast basket, measuring average global prices of coffee, sugar, wheat, and orange juice with 2015 as the baseline (indexed to 100), currently stands at 132. This represents an approximate 32% increase since 2015. The rise in the index has been uneven across items and concentrated in more recent years rather than a steady climb. This headline figure reflects aggregated price movements rather than consistent broad commodity inflation.
notes.movers: Coffee and orange juice have been the main contributors, with coffee prices up 93% and orange juice up 22% since 2015, while wheat and sugar have seen more modest increases of 7% and 5%, respectively. These price changes reflect impacts of specific weather events and crop diseases such as citrus greening and hurricanes affecting orange juice, and frost and drought in arabica coffee growing regions. These are thin global soft commodity markets, meaning supply disruptions can cause sharp price swings.
notes.why: The headline rise in the basket is primarily driven by a few weather-sensitive and disease-affected crops, rather than broad demand inflation. Given the nature of these soft commodity markets, elevated input prices can persist for years as environmental and agronomic challenges continue to impact production. Therefore, these price levels may not normalize quickly without significant changes in crop conditions.
